The paper presents an analytical approach to electromagnetic scattering from random surfaces with many scales of roughness.
The approach is based on a perturbation technique developed by Burrows.
The surface height spectrum is assumed to be jointly and Gaussian.
The surface height spectrum is split into two contiguous regions: large scale and small scale.
The condition for the large scale surface height to be sufficiently smooth is 4ko C2 >> 1.
The condition for the small scale surface height to be sufficiently small is 4ko gs << 1.
The result of the first-order perturbation analysis is a continuous description of the scattering.

The effect of the large scale surface structure on the scattering is equivalent to a convolution in k-space of the height spectrum with the shadowing function, a polarization and surface slope dependent function, and a Gaussian factor.
The condition for the large scale slopes to be small is that the large scale slopes are less than 0.1.
The value of ad computed for the numerical example is 27T cm.
The frequency dependence of the geometrical optics result is that the result increases at normal incidence and decays more rapidly with angle of incidence as the electromagnetic wavelength increases.
The effect of the large scale slope on the depolarization is that the depolarization is dependent on the large scale slope and may not be negligible, especially near grazing incidence.
The analysis is restricted to backscattering from a perfectly conducting surface.
The extension to bistatic scattering from a dielectric interface is also discussed.
The paper presents a numerical example to study the behavior of the solution as a function of the wavenumber kd.
The condition for kd to be as small as possible is that kd should be less than 0.1.
The value of kd computed for the numerical example is 27T cm.
The paper presents a comparison with conventional composite surface theory.
The paper presents a discussion of the limitations of the analysis.
